body:
**Immediate danger or a life-threatening emergency?** [Call 000 — Police, Fire or Ambulance](tel:000) {{state-block:ses-line}}
## What do you need?
Urgent help ↗Emergency calls, police assistance, poisons and nurse advice. Warnings & conditions ↗{{state-block:warnings-tile}} Bushfire readiness ↗{{state-block:bushfire-tile}} Bird flu & animals ↗Official H5 guidance and animal-disease reporting. Health & outbreaks ↗Flu, COVID-19, RSV, vaccination and public health contacts. Crisis & personal safety ↗Mental health, violence support and help for young people. After a disaster ↗{{state-block:recovery-tile}}
## Prepare before you need help [Build a household plan](/prepare), [plan for animals](/animals), and [find accessible or language support](/accessible-help). Keep important contacts somewhere you can reach without power or internet. ## Useful starting points {{resources:myfireplan,role:warnings,role:fire,birdflu}}
**Independent directory. Not a live alert service.** Records were reviewed between 14 and 18 October 2026; each card shows its own review date. Open official sources for current warnings, eligibility, opening hours and instructions. Do not use this site to decide whether an area is safe. [About this directory](/about) · [Full source register](/sources).

title: Urgent help & essential numbers
description: Know which number to call, and when to use a non-emergency service.
body:
For an immediate or life-threatening emergency, call **000**. Ask for Police, Fire or Ambulance, give your exact location and follow the call-taker’s instructions. Do not delay an emergency call to browse this directory.

## Emergency response

{{resources:triple-zero,role:ses}}

## Police assistance and health advice

These are not substitutes for emergency response. If someone is seriously ill or injured, or a crime is happening now, call **000**.

{{resources:role:police,poisons,healthdirect}}

## If a voice call is not accessible

[Accessible emergency calls and relay options](/accessible-help) explains 106 and links to the National Relay Service. **106 is for TTY/TDD emergency calls, not ordinary SMS.**

## Crisis support

For emotional distress, mental-health support or family/sexual violence support, see [crisis and personal safety](/crisis-support). If someone’s life is in immediate danger, call **000**.

title: Warnings, roads & evacuation
description: Go directly to official current information. This page does not display live alerts.

evacuation.*:
## Evacuation centres

Centres and safe routes change. Check official emergency-service channels and local emergency broadcasts for open evacuation centres. Do not travel to an assumed centre based on an old screenshot, saved copy or this directory. Follow current emergency-service directions.

levels.NSW:
## Understand warning levels

The NSW emergency hub explains three levels: **Advice**, **Watch and Act**, and **Emergency Warning**. Read the action statement, not just the colour or level. Different hazards and locations require different actions.

Source: [NSW Government — emergencies and warning information](https://www.nsw.gov.au/emergency).

get-ready.NSW: Follow [Get Ready NSW](https://www.nsw.gov.au/emergency/get-ready) to prepare communication backups.

title: Bushfire: prepare early

description.NSW: NSW Rural Fire Service information, fire danger ratings and household planning.
description.*: {{term:fire}} information, fire danger ratings and household planning.

ratings.NSW: A fire danger rating describes the possible consequences **if a fire starts**. It is different from an incident warning. Check both the rating and current incident advice.

myfireplan.NSW: MyFirePlan is an external NSW RFS tool; this directory does not assess whether your home is defendable. Leaving early is your safest choice.
myfireplan.*: Use {{term:fire}} bushfire planning guidance to make your plan. This directory does not assess whether your home is defendable.

title: Bird flu & biosecurity
description: Official H5 bird flu guidance for wildlife, households, pets and farms.
body:
## Report concerns safely

{{resources:birdflu}}

## Find guidance for your situation

The official hub links to guidance for:

- Pets, backyard chickens and other birds.
- Wildlife and wildlife carers.
- Poultry and livestock farmers, and vets.
- First Nations communities.
- Human health, translated resources and local state/territory advice.

Use the [Australian Government bird flu hub](https://birdflu.gov.au/) for those pathways. It redirects to [DAFF’s H5 campaign](https://www.agriculture.gov.au/campaigns/birdflu).

## Current status belongs on the official source

Outbreak status, restrictions and reporting data change. This directory deliberately does **not** reproduce case totals, declare an area disease-free or provide animal-handling or treatment instructions. Check current local advice through the official hub.

For a human medical emergency, call **000**. For non-emergency health advice, [healthdirect: 1800 022 222](tel:1800022222).

## Animal evacuation planning is a separate task

[Plan for pets, livestock and assistance animals](/animals) before an evacuation. Do not transport potentially infected wildlife or animals on the basis of this directory; ask the reporting service or a vet for situation-specific directions.

title: Health, flu & outbreaks
description: Official {{state}} and Australian information on flu, COVID-19, RSV, vaccination and public health.

respiratory.NSW: NSW Health’s respiratory illness guidance centres on vaccination, staying home when unwell, wearing a mask if you must go out, and avoiding crowded or poorly ventilated spaces. It also suggests considering a rapid antigen test before visiting people at higher risk, and making a plan with your doctor if you are at higher risk of severe illness.

directions.NSW: If a new outbreak or pandemic response is announced, follow NSW Health and Australian Government directions.
directions.*: If a new outbreak or pandemic response is announced, follow {{term:health}} and Australian Government directions.

body:
**Medical emergency?** Call **000**. This page links to official health information and is not medical advice.
## Unwell and unsure what to do? {{resources:healthdirect}} ## Flu, COVID-19 and RSV {{state-block:respiratory}} {{resources:nsw-respiratory,covid-info}} ## Vaccination Ask your GP, pharmacist or Aboriginal Medical Service which vaccines and timing suit you. Eligibility for free vaccines changes, so check the official pages below rather than a copy here. {{resources:flu-vaccine,covid-vaccine,nsw-immunisation}} ## Outbreaks and public health {{resources:role:health,nsw-phu}} For H5 bird flu, which is an animal-disease issue, use [Bird flu & biosecurity](/bird-flu). ## Old numbers and current status The former National Coronavirus Helpline (1800 020 080) is no longer in service, but it still appears on older printed material and some websites. Use the healthdirect helpline or your GP instead. This directory deliberately does **not** reproduce case numbers, outbreak totals, testing or antiviral eligibility, or public health orders.{{state-block:directions}}

body:
## Start with official planning resources

{{resources:get-ready,rfs-plan}}

{{state-block:get-ready}}

## Discuss these needs before an emergency

- Who needs help, and who can provide it if the usual carer is unavailable?
- Where will you go, how will you travel, and what is your backup route?
- How will you receive warnings and contact people if power or mobile service fails?
- What medicines, documents, equipment and supplies need to leave with you?
- How will you move pets, livestock or assistance animals safely?

These are planning prompts, not an evacuation order or a complete kit specification. {{state-block:checklists}}

## Choose the relevant pathway

{{state-block:pathways}}

## Save essential contacts

Print the [urgent-help page](/urgent-help) and your household's plan. The Site's page menu offers PDF export for printing, or use your browser's Print function. A printout is a backup reference; current warnings still come from official services.

## Make animal arrangements early

{{resources:get-ready-animals,pets,assistance-animals}}

Check current evacuation-centre arrangements and identify suitable alternatives for animals. {{state-block:assistance-animals}}Never re-enter an unsafe location to retrieve an animal.

## Sick or dead birds and wildlife

For suspected bird flu, [open the official H5 reporting guidance](/bird-flu). Do not touch or closely approach sick or dead birds or other animals. The Emergency Animal Disease Hotline is **1800 675 888**.

## How this directory was checked

Resource names, contact details and summaries were reviewed against government, emergency-service or service-provider pages. Records were reviewed between 14 and 18 October 2026; each card shows its own review date. Hours appear only where supported by the cited research. A review date is not a guarantee of continuing accuracy or current service availability.

Each entry links directly to its official source.{{state-block:explicit}} The bird flu short address redirects to DAFF’s H5 campaign.

The source project includes machine-readable resource data, research notes and test reports. You can also download the [resource register as JSON](/resources.json).

## Full register

Records are grouped below: national services first, then the main state, then every other state and territory.

{{all-resources}}

## Technical references

[Blume quickstart](https://useblume.dev/docs/quickstart) · [Blume deployment](https://useblume.dev/docs/deployment) · [Cloudflare Pages direct upload](https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/get-started/direct-upload/) · [Cloudflare Workers static assets](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/).

## Maintaining accuracy

Review urgent phone numbers and URLs regularly and after any agency restructure or announced service change. Treat a network failure during link checking as unverified, not proof that a service has closed. Check changed content manually before changing the directory.

title: About this directory
description: An independent reference, not an emergency service or live warning feed.
body:
## Purpose and scope

Emergency Ready brings together Australian national contacts and {{state}} emergency resources. {{state}}-specific numbers, planning resources and recovery pathways are labelled. It is not a complete directory of every state, council or utility service. Pages on urgent help, warnings, bushfire, preparing, health, crisis support and recovery end with core services for the other states and territories, and the [sources page](/sources) lists every resource in this build.

## Important limitations

- This site is **independent** and is not operated or endorsed by government or the linked services.
- It does not receive emergency requests, dispatch help, provide medical/legal advice or assess whether a route or location is safe.
- It does not display live warnings. Use official current sources and emergency-service directions.
- Links, hours, eligibility and service arrangements can change after the review date.
- For immediate danger or a life-threatening emergency, call **000**.

## Privacy and safety

The site has no analytics, advertising, account signup, embedded third-party maps or AI advice assistant. Search runs locally in your browser after its index loads. Fonts are hosted with the site. Hosting providers can still process ordinary request logs, and external resources have their own privacy policies.

Your browser may remember visits and preferences, and device/network records may remain. This is **not** a private browsing or quick-exit tool. See [personal safety considerations](/crisis-support).

## Offline and printing

Important content is static HTML and can be read with JavaScript disabled. Search and mobile drawer interactions need JavaScript; an always-visible page directory is provided below for a no-script fallback. The deployed site does not install a service worker or promise offline access. Save or print essential details in advance and open current official warnings when connected.

## Page directory

[Start](/) · [Urgent help](/urgent-help) · [Warnings](/warnings) · [Bushfire](/bushfire) · [Bird flu](/bird-flu) · [Health & outbreaks](/health) · [Crisis support](/crisis-support) · [Prepare](/prepare) · [Accessible help](/accessible-help) · [Animals](/animals) · [Recovery](/recovery) · [Sources](/sources).

## Corrections and maintenance

To report a wrong, missing or out-of-date contact or link, open an issue on the project’s [GitHub repository](https://github.com/halans/nsw-emergency-guide/issues). Do not include personal or sensitive information, and do not use GitHub to ask for emergency help: call **000**. The site itself has no backend or reporting inbox. Maintainers can edit the resource register and page templates, run the documented checks and rebuild.

[Sources and review policy](/sources).
